newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Major airline companies are cancelling or severely curtailing their routes to Greece as part of a worldwide trend to cut back on operating costs. After 50 years of the Greek scene, TWA will end flights to Greece as of April 18, sources say, while Lufthansa and others' flights to Thessaloniki are also in danger. Tourism, of course, will be hardest hit.

--The stability of the drachma's parity against the Ecu to bolster the anti-inflationary effort is the main aim of foreign exchange policy to this year, a meeting between National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou and Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos decided yesterday.
--At least another two bids for the Bank of Crete are expected to be submitted by the deadline later today. Reports say there has been great interest in the sale so far.
--The finance ministry is to establish a special department to deal with electronic tax evasion, following reports of 'smart' cash registers.
IMERISIA

--High levels of fluidity is worrying the Bank of Greece, which is intervening on a daily basis on the market to deal with the problem. The one trillion drachmas, sources say, comes from foreign capital inflows and from the conversion into drachmas of foreign loans in December to cover the servicing of the debt and poses a problem for inflation in the medium-term.

--Foreign investors have sent a message of intense interest in a possible new Greek telecoms organisation (OTE) share offer, buying 100,000 shares yesterday. Prices closed at 4,940 drachmas, up 6.2 percent.

--The first half of 1997 is considered cruical for achieving the government's target of 5.5 percent inflation by the end of the year. The consumer price index is expected to fall to 7.1 percent from today's 7.5 percent, with February being the month it breaks through the 7.0 percent barrier. In June, the government hopes inflation will stand at around 6.0 percent.
KERDOS

--The government is basing the increase in revenues on a three-year denationalisation programme to involve 50 organisations and firms in the wider public sphere. On the list, sources say, are profit-makers such as Duty-Free Stores and medium-range banks.
--The finance ministry is offering debtors another chance to pay off debts to the state with favourable terms.
--The Bank of Attica is drafting a new five-year business plan that will involve the bank tranforming itself into a general bank with emphasis on the construction sector and regional development.

--The 'Zeus' consortium of advertising companies - led by Adel Saatchi & Saatchi - was awarded the Greek National Tourism Organisation (EOT) overseas advertising campaign for 1997 on the strength of new slogan "Greece: The Authentic Story". Leo Burnett received the public relations programme.
EXPRESS

--Car insurance premiums based on social and geographical criteria are being proposed by leading private sector insurance firms and appear to have been accepted by state insurance firms. Premium tariffs will be decided by the end of the month.
--Subsidies of up to 10 billion drachmas are soon to be distributed to small- and medium-size enterprises, the first tranche of the 100 billion drachmas for SMEs up to the year 2000.
--Retail prices on cigarettes will be increased by at least 9.0 percent as of January 20.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Foreign capital inflows of 1.5 billion dollars in the first 10 days of the year - 850 billion of which are EU inflows - are considered to be a positive development despite the high amount creating problems in the exercise of monetary policy.
--The Bank of Greece has recommended to the finance ministry that it further exploit the opportunities afforded by international markets to cover the external public debt.
--Conservative opposition New Democracy will request a copy of the audit into ASE brokerage firms. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
